titulo_es: Impersonal passive (It is said that… / He is said to…)
descripcion_es: Reporting opinions and rumours without saying who holds them: it is said that, he is believed to have…
resumen: With verbs such as say, believe, think, report, expect, know or consider, formal English (the press, reports) presents what “people say” or “people believe” with two structures: It is said that + clause, or subject + is said + to + infinitive.

filas: It + be + past participle + that + clause
It is said that the castle is haunted.
People say that the castle is haunted. (es: Se dice que el castillo está encantado.)
Subject + be + past participle + to + infinitive
The castle is said to be haunted.
People say that the castle is haunted. (es: Se dice que el castillo está encantado.)
The minister is thought to be considering resigning.
People think the minister is considering resigning. (es: Se cree que el ministro está pensando en dimitir.)
The thieves are believed to have escaped abroad.
People believe the thieves have escaped abroad. (es: Se cree que los ladrones han huido al extranjero.)
There are reported to be ten victims.
It is reported that there are ten victims. (es: Se informa de que hay diez víctimas.)

explicacion.texto: How to choose the infinitive: if what is said happens at the same time as the saying, use to + infinitive (or to be + -ing); if it happened earlier, use to have + past participle. People say he lived in Paris → He is said to have lived in Paris.
If the verb of opinion is in the past, be changes: People thought she was rich → She was thought to be rich / It was thought that she was rich.

items: Verbos habituales: say, think, believe, report, expect, know, consider, claim, understand, allege, estimate.
It is typical of the press and reports: The economy is expected to grow by 2%.
It is not translated with Spanish “se” + an active verb in English: not “It says that…” in the sense of Spanish “se dice”.

ejemplos.frase: It is widely believed that the policy has failed.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se cree ampliamente que la política ha fracasado.

ejemplos.frase: The painting is thought to be worth over a million euros.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se cree que el cuadro vale más de un millón de euros.

ejemplos.frase: Unemployment is expected to fall next year.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se espera que el paro baje el año que viene.

ejemplos.frase: The singer is reported to have cancelled her tour.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se informa de que la cantante ha cancelado su gira.

ejemplos.frase: It was known that the bridge needed repairs.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se sabía que el puente necesitaba reparaciones.

ejemplos.frase: Two climbers are said to be missing on the mountain.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se dice que hay dos escaladores desaparecidos en la montaña.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: It is said he to be very rich.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: He is said to be very rich.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Either It is said that he is…, or He is said to be…; the two are not mixed.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She is believed to leave the country last week.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: She is believed to have left the country last week.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Action earlier than the moment of believing: to have + past participle.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Is said that prices will rise.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: It is said that prices will rise.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: The new stadium is expected ___ (open) next spring.
respuestas: to open
ejercicios.explicacion: The second row of the table applies: subject + be + past participle + to + infinitive. The clue is that the sentence already begins with a specific subject (the new stadium) followed by is expected, so that + clause does not fit, only to + infinitive. As the opening comes after the moment of expecting, the simple infinitive is enough: to open.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se espera que el nuevo estadio abra la próxima primavera.

errores_previstos.respuesta: opening
errores_previstos.explicacion: Be expected is followed by to + infinitive, not the -ing form.

errores_previstos.respuesta: that it opens
errores_previstos.explicacion: With a personal subject in front (the new stadium is expected) you don't use that; that option only works with It is expected that…

errores_previstos.respuesta: to have opened
errores_previstos.explicacion: To have + past participle indicates something earlier than the moment of expecting, and the opening is in the future (next spring).

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: The fire is believed ___ (start) in the kitchen last night.
respuestas: to have started
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule in Rules and key points for choosing the infinitive applies: if what is believed happened before the moment of believing it, use to have + past participle. The clue is last night: the fire started before now, when it is believed. That is why it is to have started, with the regular past participle of start.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Earlier action: to have + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se cree que el incendio empezó en la cocina anoche.

errores_previstos.respuesta: to start
errores_previstos.explicacion: The simple infinitive indicates something simultaneous or future; with last night you need to have started.

errores_previstos.respuesta: to have start
errores_previstos.explicacion: To have is followed by the past participle, started.

errores_previstos.respuesta: started
errores_previstos.explicacion: After is believed with a personal subject you need to + infinitive.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: The president is understood ___ (prepare) a major speech at this moment.
respuestas: to be preparing
ejercicios.explicacion: The third row of the table applies: … to be + -ing for an action in progress. The clue is at this moment, which indicates that the preparation is happening now, at the same time as it is understood. That is why to prepare is not enough and you need to be preparing, just as in The minister is thought to be considering resigning.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se entiende que el presidente está preparando un discurso importante en este momento.

errores_previstos.respuesta: to prepare
errores_previstos.explicacion: The simple infinitive does not express the action in progress marked by at this moment; you need to be preparing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: to be prepared
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is passive (“to be prepared”), and the president is the one preparing the speech.

errores_previstos.respuesta: preparing
errores_previstos.explicacion: After is understood with a personal subject, to be is missing.

ejercicios.frase: ___ is reported that the talks have broken down.
respuestas: It
ejercicios.explicacion: The first row of the table applies: It + be + past participle + that + clause. The clue is that the gap is followed by is reported that and a complete clause with its own subject (the talks). English requires a grammatical subject in the main clause, and in this structure it is the empty it. Remember the third typical mistake: “Is said that…” without it is incorrect.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Structure It is reported that + clause.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se informa de que las negociaciones se han roto.

errores_previstos.respuesta: There
errores_previstos.explicacion: There is used with to be (There are reported to be…), not with that + clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: This
errores_previstos.explicacion: This would point to something specific; the impersonal structure uses the empty subject it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He
errores_previstos.explicacion: A personal subject would require to + infinitive (He is reported to…), not that.

ejercicios.frase: Shakespeare is thought ___ this play around 1600.
respuestas: to have written
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for choosing the infinitive applies: if the fact is earlier than the moment of thinking it, use to have + past participle. The clue is around 1600: the writing happened long before today, when it is thought. That is why it is to have written, with the irregular past participle of write.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A fact earlier than the moment of thinking: to have + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se cree que Shakespeare escribió esta obra hacia 1600.

por_opcion.to have written: Correct: perfect infinitive for a fact earlier than the moment of thinking.
por_opcion.to write: Incorrect: the simple infinitive would indicate simultaneity or the future, as if he were writing it now.
por_opcion.that he wrote: Incorrect: with a personal subject (Shakespeare is thought) you don't use that; it would be It is thought that he wrote…
por_opcion.writing: Incorrect: after is thought with a personal subject comes to + infinitive, never -ing.

ejercicios.frase: There ___ to be over a thousand people at the protest.
respuestas: were said
ejercicios.explicacion: The last row of the table applies: There + be + past participle + to be. The clue is There at the start and to be right after the gap. Be agrees with what follows, over a thousand people, which is plural, and the sentence is in the past, hence were said.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: There + be + past participle + to be; plural because of a thousand people.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se dijo que había más de mil personas en la manifestación.

por_opcion.were said: Correct: passive in the past and in the plural, agreeing with a thousand people.
por_opcion.said: Incorrect: it is active and there cannot be the subject of say; be is missing.
por_opcion.was saying: Incorrect: it is active continuous and singular; it would mean “there was saying”.

ejercicios.frase: It ___ that the company will announce job cuts.
respuestas: is rumoured
ejercicios.explicacion: The first row of the table applies: It + be + past participle + that + clause. The clue is It at the start and that after the gap. Rumour is used almost only in the passive with this meaning (Spanish “se rumorea”), which is why it is is rumoured. Rumoured is the British spelling; in American English it is spelt rumored.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se rumorea que la empresa anunciará recortes de plantilla.

por_opcion.rumours: Incorrect: it is active and would mean that it spreads a rumour; in English a thing does not “rumour”.
por_opcion.is rumouring: Incorrect: it is active continuous, which does not exist with this verb and this meaning.

ejercicios.frase: He is said that he is a brilliant pianist.
respuestas: He is said to be a brilliant pianist.
It is said that he is a brilliant pianist.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule of not mixing the two structures applies, which is the first typical mistake in this unit. The clue is that the sentence begins with a personal subject (He is said), which means it must continue with to + infinitive: to be a brilliant pianist. You can also change the subject to it and keep that: It is said that he is a brilliant pianist.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With a personal subject you use to + infinitive, not that.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se dice que es un pianista brillante.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He is said that he is a brilliant pianist.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: with a personal subject you don't use that.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He is said to is a brilliant pianist.
errores_previstos.explicacion: To is followed by the infinitive be.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It is said he to be a brilliant pianist.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It mixes the two structures: either It is said that he is…, or He is said to be…

ejercicios.frase: The suspect is thought to escape through the window yesterday.
respuestas: The suspect is thought to have escaped through the window yesterday.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule for choosing the infinitive applies: for an action earlier than the moment of thinking, use to have + past participle. The clue is yesterday, which places the escape before now. With to escape the sentence would say that the suspect is thinking of escaping; you need to have escaped.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Earlier action: to have + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se cree que el sospechoso escapó ayer por la ventana.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The suspect is thought to escape through the window yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: with yesterday you need to have escaped.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The suspect is thought to have escape through the window yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: To have is followed by the past participle escaped.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The suspect is thought to escaped through the window yesterday.
errores_previstos.explicacion: To cannot be followed by the past tense; for an earlier action you need to have escaped.

ejercicios.frase: Is believed that the treasure is buried here.
respuestas: It is believed that the treasure is buried here.
ejercicios.explicacion: The first row of the table and the third typical mistake apply: English needs a subject, and in this structure it is It. The clue is that the sentence begins directly with Is believed that, a calque of Spanish “se cree que”. You just need to add It at the start.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se cree que el tesoro está enterrado aquí.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Is believed that the treasure is buried here.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This copies the sentence without correcting it: the subject It is missing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It believes that the treasure is buried here.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is active and would mean that “it believes”; the impersonal structure is passive: It is believed.

errores_previstos.respuesta: There is believed that the treasure is buried here.
errores_previstos.explicacion: There is not used with that + clause; the empty subject is It.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence beginning with The company.
ejercicios.frase: People say that the company is losing money.
respuestas: The company is said to be losing money.
ejercicios.explicacion: The third row of the table applies: subject + is said + to be + -ing for an action in progress. The clue is is losing in the original sentence, a present continuous: the loss of money is happening now, while it is being said. As the instruction requires you to begin with The company, the structure is the personal one, with a continuous to-infinitive.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Action in progress: is said to be + -ing.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se dice que la empresa está perdiendo dinero.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The company is said to lose money.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The simple infinitive loses the continuous aspect of is losing; you need to be losing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The company is said that it is losing money.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With a personal subject you don't use that.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The company says to be losing money.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is active: it would mean that the company says something. You need is said.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence beginning with It.
ejercicios.frase: Experts expect that house prices will rise.
respuestas: It is expected that house prices will rise.
It's expected that house prices will rise.
ejercicios.explicacion: The first row of the table applies: It + be + past participle + that + clause. The clue is the instruction, which requires you to begin with It, and experts expect, a generic subject that is left out. The subordinate clause (house prices will rise) stays intact after that. The contraction It's is also acceptable.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: It + is + past participle + that + clause.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se espera que los precios de la vivienda suban.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It is expected house prices to rise.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It mixes the two structures; It goes with that + a complete clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It expects that house prices will rise.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is active; the impersonal structure is It is expected.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It is expect that house prices will rise.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Is is followed by the past participle expected.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence beginning with The thief.
ejercicios.frase: Police believe that the thief entered through the roof.
respuestas: The thief is believed to have entered through the roof.
ejercicios.explicacion: The fourth row of the table applies: … to have + past participle for an earlier action. The clue is entered, in the past: the entry happened before the moment when the police believe it. As the sentence begins with The thief, the structure is personal: is believed to have entered.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Earlier action: is believed to have + past participle.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se cree que el ladrón entró por el tejado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The thief is believed to enter through the roof.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The simple infinitive does not indicate that the entry came earlier; you need to have entered.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The thief is believed that he entered through the roof.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With a personal subject you don't use that.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The thief was believed to have entered through the roof.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Believe is in the present in the original (police believe): is believed.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence beginning with She.
ejercicios.frase: People thought that she was a spy.
respuestas: She was thought to be a spy.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule in this unit applies: if the verb of opinion is in the past, be changes (was thought). The clue is thought, the past of think, in the original. What was thought (being a spy) was simultaneous with the thinking, so to be is enough. The personal subject she requires the structure with to + infinitive.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Verb of opinion in the past: was thought + to be.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She is thought to be a spy.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb of opinion is in the past in the original: was thought.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She was thought to have been a spy.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The perfect infinitive would indicate that she was a spy before they thought it; here it is simultaneous: to be.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She was thought that she was a spy.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With a personal subject you don't use that.

respuestas: the house is said to be haunted
is the house said to be haunted
ejercicios.explicacion: The second row of the table applies: subject + is said + to + infinitive. The clue is that the words include said, to and be, but not that, which requires the personal structure. Haunted is an adjective and goes after be. The question form, with is before the subject, is also acceptable.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se dice que la casa está encantada.

errores_previstos.respuesta: is said the house to be haunted
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “se dice la casa…”: the subject goes first, the house is said…

errores_previstos.respuesta: the house is said be to haunted
errores_previstos.explicacion: The infinitive is to be, in that order.

respuestas: it is known that smoking kills
is it known that smoking kills
ejercicios.explicacion: The first row of the table applies: It + be + past participle + that + clause. The clue is that the words include it and that. That is followed by the complete clause, with smoking as the subject (gerund) and kills as the verb. The question form inverts is and it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: is known that smoking kills it
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is the empty subject of the main clause and goes at the beginning, not at the end.

errores_previstos.respuesta: it is known smoking that kills
errores_previstos.explicacion: That introduces the whole clause and goes before its subject smoking.

descripcion_larga_es: The impersonal passive (It is said that…, He is said to…) is the way formal English presents rumours, opinions and forecasts without attributing them to anyone in particular: Spanish “se dice”, “se cree”, “se espera”. It dominates the press, economic reports and academic texts. Spanish speakers find it difficult because Spanish solves everything with “se” and because you have to choose the right infinitive (to be, to be doing, to have done).

contexto.que_es: They are two structures with verbs of opinion or information (say, think, believe, expect, report, know…): It + be + past participle + that + clause, or subject + be + past participle + to + infinitive. Both are equivalent to Spanish “se dice que”, “se cree que”, “se espera que”.
contexto.por_que_importa: They let you pass on information with distance and caution, something essential in journalism, reports and any professional text in which you don't want to state something as your own view. Using them wrongly produces very visible ungrammatical sentences, such as mixing the two structures or forgetting the subject it. In an exam at B2 level or above it is a classic transformation item.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When quoting rumours, estimates, forecasts or general beliefs: The suspect is believed to have fled, Prices are expected to rise. The signs are verbs such as say, believe, report or expect and a generic subject in the active sentence (people, experts, police). Spanish speakers tend to calque “se dice” with “Is said” without a subject, or with “It says”, which means something else (“the text says”).
